planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring into well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; Bigun forms a tight dwarf clump that fills in faster than standard border liriope, so tighter spacing is workable for quick coverage.

directions: Bigun, marketed under the trade name Cleopatra, is a patented dwarf selection of Liriope muscari — an open-pollinated seedling of 'Big Blue' — valued for dense, dark green foliage that stays noticeably shorter than standard border lilyturf. Lavender flower spikes rise above the clump in summer and give way to black berries that persist into fall. It handles summer heat and humidity reliably and forms an even, well-behaved clump rather than spreading aggressively, making it useful for edging and mass plantings where a compact scale is wanted. Divide crowded clumps in early spring every several years to maintain a tidy habit.
sources: JC Raulston Arboretum, NC State University

common_name: Shiroshima Ryu Mondo Grass (Dramatic White-Striped Dwarf Mondo Grass)

planting.note: Set small divisions in spring into humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in filtered sun to full shade; this cultivar spreads slowly like other mondo grass, so allow extra time to fill in as a solid groundcover mass.

directions: Shiroshima Ryu is a Japanese selection of dwarf mondo grass grown for bold, vertical white striping that runs the length of each slender, dark green blade, giving a brighter and more dramatic variegation than older striped mondo selections. It forms a low, dense, arching clump and spreads gradually by short rhizomes, making it a good fine-textured accent for lightening dark woodland corners or edging shaded paths. Small white to pale lilac bell-shaped flowers appear on short stalks in summer but are secondary to the foliage display. Keep soil consistently moist for the best color and fullest growth, since this selection is slower to establish than plain green mondo grass.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Little Jess Flax Lily (Compact Blue Flax Lily)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to moderate shade; Little Jess stays compact and dense, so it needs little grooming or division compared with larger flax lily selections.

directions: Little Jess is a compact, protected-variety selection of Dianella caerulea bred in Australia for a dense, dwarf habit of arching deep green strap-like leaves, noticeably smaller than species-type blue flax lily. Pale blue star-shaped flowers appear on short stalks in spring, followed by small blue-purple berries. It is markedly drought tolerant once established and needs little more than an occasional tidy-up rather than regular cutting back, holding its neat clumping form for years. Use it for edging, mass planting, or containers where a true dwarf flax lily habit is wanted.
sources: Australian native plant nursery trade listings

common_name: Breeze Flax Lily (Dark Green Low-Maintenance Blue Flax Lily)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Breeze's short flower stalks keep spent bloom debris to a minimum, reducing the need for post-bloom tidying that taller flax lilies require.

directions: Breeze is an Australian-bred selection of Dianella caerulea with free-flowing, dark green, sword-shaped foliage and a notably fast fill rate compared with older flax lily selections. Blue and yellow flowers appear in spring and often develop into showy purple berries, but the flower stalks stay short, so the plant avoids the tall, messy dead canes that can disfigure other dianellas after bloom. It is tolerant of drought, frost, and coastal salt exposure once established and needs little regular maintenance. Use it for mass landscape planting, screening low borders, or erosion-prone slopes.
sources: Australian native plant nursery trade listings

common_name: Baby Breeze Flax Lily (Dwarf Bright-Green Compact Flax Lily)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring with the crown held slightly above soil level to avoid waterlogging; Baby Breeze tolerates sand or clay but benefits from good drainage at the crown while establishing.

directions: Baby Breeze is a dwarf sibling selection of the larger Breeze flax lily, bred for a smaller scale while keeping the same low-maintenance, slow-to-flower-stalk habit. Its leaves are broader and a brighter fresh green than typical blue-gray-toned flax lilies, and masses of small blue-purple star-shaped flowers appear in spring and summer, followed by metallic blue berries that attract birds. It tolerates sun, shade, and frost once established and needs minimal grooming, making it well suited to small-scale borders and edging where the standard-size Breeze would be too large. Keep soil on the drier side once roots are established, since it is quite drought tolerant.
sources: Australian native plant nursery trade listings

common_name: King Alfred Flax Lily (Late-Blooming Salt-Tolerant Blue Flax Lily)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring into well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; King Alfred tolerates coastal salt spray and salty irrigation water better than most flax lily selections, making it a strong choice near beaches or reclaimed-water sites.

directions: King Alfred was discovered as a single standout seedling in a large batch of Dianella caerulea 'Sydney Ecotype' grown at a New South Wales nursery, selected for a dense, compact clumping habit of narrow blue-green strappy foliage. It blooms later in the season than most other flax lily selections and the pale violet-blue flowers linger longer before giving way to bright purple berries. It is notably tolerant of wet feet, greywater irrigation, and salt-laden coastal winds, and also handles dry spells and humidity well once established. Use it for coastal landscaping, soil-stabilizing mass plantings, or anywhere a tough, dual-purpose ornamental groundcover is needed.
sources: UC Landscape Plant Irrigation Trials (UC ANR)

common_name: Allyn Citation Flax Lily (Coolvista Compact Gray-Green Flax Lily)

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in spring into lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; its small, upright habit suits tight border spacing compared with larger flax lily selections.

directions: Allyn-Citation, sold under the trade name Coolvista, is a patented compact selection of Dianella revoluta bred by Noel Jupp of East Gresford, New South Wales, from a controlled cross between two unnamed, unpatented Dianella revoluta selections. Royal blue berries follow modest spring flowers, adding understated seasonal interest above the stiff, fan-like clump of narrow, upright, spiky gray-green foliage. It is markedly drought tolerant once rooted in and holds its tidy, compact form without the floppy or splitting habit that can affect larger flax lily types. Its small scale and tough constitution make it well suited to rock gardens, tight borders, and low-water landscape plantings.
